privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This app is a personal, non-commercial project for a group of friends competing on World Cup 2026 predictions. We want to be clear and honest about what data we store and why.
privacy.section1Email: Email: needed to create your account, log in, and send the verification email.
privacy.section1Username: Username: the one you pick when signing up. It's shown to other players in pools you join.
privacy.section1Password: Password: stored hashed. We can't read it in plain text either.
privacy.section1Predictions: Predictions and results: every score you submit, along with the points you earn.
privacy.section1Groups: Pools you participate in: the groups you joined or created.
privacy.section1Note: We do NOT store: location, phone number, payment info, or any other personal data. We don't use Google Analytics or any other tracking service.
privacy.section2Body: Only to make the app work: authenticate you, show your predictions, calculate your rank, and email you account-related stuff (verification, password reset).
privacy.section3Intro: We use two technical providers to run the app:
privacy.section3Supabase: Supabase (United States): stores the database, handles authentication, and sends verification emails.
privacy.section3Note: We don't share your data with advertisers, third parties, or anyone beyond the technical providers we need.
privacy.section4Body: As long as your account is active. If you ask us to delete it, we will. There's no automatic deletion for inactivity — but if you want to disappear, just let us know.
privacy.section5Intro: You can ask at any time to:
privacy.section5Right1: See what data we have about you.
privacy.section5Right3: Delete your account and all associated data.
privacy.section6Body: Email us at <mail>{{email}}</mail>. It's the project owner's address. We'll reply as fast as we can.
privacy.section7Body: We only use the session cookies set by Supabase to keep you logged in. No tracking, advertising, or third-party cookies.

rules.title: Rules
rules.subtitle: How to play and how scoring works
rules.intro: This pool is between friends: you predict the scores of all 104 matches of the 2026 World Cup and earn points based on how close you get. Whoever racks up the most points wins. Simple as that.
rules.how1: Create a pool or join a friend's with the invite code.
rules.how2: Before each match, submit your prediction: how many goals each team scores.
rules.how3: When the match ends, the app calculates your points automatically and updates the ranking.
rules.scoringExact: Exact score: you nailed the result (e.g. you predicted 2-1 and it ended 2-1).
rules.scoringResult: Correct result: you got the winner or draw right, but not the exact score (e.g. you predicted 2-0 and it ended 1-0).
rules.scoringMiss: Missed: you didn't even get the winner right.
rules.scoringExample: Example: if you predict 3-1 and the match ends 2-0, you get 1 point because you correctly called the home win, even without the exact score.
rules.lockBody: You can submit and edit your prediction until the exact moment the match kicks off. Once it starts, it's locked and can't be changed. This applies to everyone equally and isn't enforced by the browser: it's protected at the database level.
rules.visibilityBody: You can't see what other participants predicted until the match kicks off. Only then is everyone's prediction revealed. That way nobody copies.
rules.rankingBody: The ranking is sorted by total points and updates in real time. If two players are tied on points, whoever has more exact scores ranks higher; if still tied, whoever has more correct results.
rules.fairBody: This is just for fun. The app doesn't manage prizes: if your group plays for something, that's between you. Play fair and may the best football mind win.
